title: APTEL: Solar Developer Without Written Force Majeure Notice Can't Escape Delay Damages, Tariff Claim Remanded
case_name: Jayamal Energy LLP v. Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission
card_summary: APTEL upheld KERC's finding that a 2 MW solar developer owed delay damages to BESCOM, because the developer never gave the written force majeure notice the power purchase agreement required to excuse the delay. On the developer's separate claim for a higher tariff of about Rs 8.40 per unit, the Tribunal declined to fix the rate itself and sent that part back to KERC.
card_tip: A force majeure defence under a solar PPA fails without a contemporaneous written notice to the procurer; verbal or after-the-fact claims of delay will not excuse liquidated damages.
verification_notes: Case facts and outcome (delay damages upheld, tariff claim remanded) corroborated by both Mercom India and SolarQuarter reports, both dated 27 October 2026; no neutral/appeal citation number was given in either report.
